info.title: Delphi.science
info.description: Index of papers, preprints, and formal proofs linked to post-publication technical responses (arXiv replies, blog posts, talks, MathOverflow, X posts) with author, date, and verbatim excerpts. Research read endpoints require no authentication; usage statistics require administrator access. Also available as an MCP server at https://delphi.science/mcp, with the same reads and writes as tools (reading needs no key; clients can sign a person in by OAuth). Guide: https://delphi.science/llms.txt

get.description: Search the index with arXiv-style queries. Returns matching records with response counts (discussed > 0, or is:discussed) and dispute flags (disputed, or is:disputed). Returns one page of records with page URL and discussed response count; pass fields=full or get a record for its full discussion[]. Covers records indexed in Delphi.science (AI-generated research releases, Lean formalizations, and this year's arXiv preprints in math, quant-ph, and hep-th). An empty q lists records newest first; q "is:discussed" with sort=responded lists the records with the newest expert responses, each with latest_response. With in=forum it searches the research forum's topics instead, by plain words.

schema.description: For records: arXiv-style query. ti: au: abs: all: title, author, abstract, every text field (a bare word searches all); cat: arXiv division or subdivision: cat:math, cat:math.NT, cat:quant-ph, or a subject name in quotes; source: category: origin: family: id: exact values, e.g. source:openai-math id:app/APP-260923-0000; is: formalized, verified, withdrawn, agent-ready, ai-generated, app, gone, discussed, disputed; published: published:[2026-10-01 TO *], published:2026-09. AND, OR, ANDNOT, NOT (uppercase), parentheses, "quoted phrases", word* prefixes; adjacent terms are ANDed. Empty lists everything. For the forum (in=forum): plain words to find in topics and replies ("quoted phrases", -excluded words).

parameters.name: in
parameters.description: records: the indexed papers, preprints and proofs. forum: the research forum's topics.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Records only. relevance (default with a query), newest (default without), oldest, title, score (votes plus linked responses that confirm, simplify or extend it or have no stance yet, all time), day, week, month (votes and such responses published in that window), mentions (most cited in comments: how many people's comments name the record by id, then the newest; not linked posts, which count in score), responded (the newest expert response first, whatever its stance).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Results per page, from 1 to 100; 20 if left out.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, from 1 to 10000, of limit items each; pages in the reply says how many there are. Ignored when cursor is given.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: next_cursor from the previous reply, unchanged.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Records only. full returns each record whole, with discussion[].

200.description: One page of records, or with in=forum of topics

400.description: Error with a code, a message and a fix

401.description: Error with a code, a message and a fix

get.summary: Get one thing by its path
get.description: Fetch one thing on Delphi.science by its path. A record id (arxiv/2610.20058): Fetch a single record: metadata, votes, reviewed reception summary, discussion[] (linked technical responses with author, date, quote, and stance), and discusses[] (records this item responds to). Response quote fields are short verbatim excerpts (open url for the full text); an empty discussion[] means no responses have been linked yet. forum/<number>: a forum topic with its opening post, answers and comments. A post's path (as log shows it): that post in full, with the revision edit needs. me: the signed-in account and how its votes and posts are signed (needs sign-in; everything else here does not).

schema.description: What to fetch, or me. A path: a record id (arxiv/2610.20058), a post on it (arxiv/2610.20058/481), forum, a forum topic (forum/12) or a post in it (forum/12/502).

200.description: The record, topic, post or account

400.description: Error with a code, a message and a fix

get.description: List what happened on Delphi.science itself, one line each, in the order it happened: records entering the index, and posts (comments and reviews on records, forum questions, answers and comments). Each line: seq, kind, path, parent, author, time, score, subject, the text cut short, and the records a post names. path narrows it to one record's thread, one source, the forum, or one topic; q narrows it by a query, so a saved query is a feed (q "cat:quant-ph" is new quant-ph records and the discussion about them) and q "to:@me" is the signed-in person's inbox (the only use that needs sign-in). Without since, the newest first; with since, what came after that seq, oldest first, so it can be followed: keep the reply's since and send it next time. Empty when there is nothing. (Responses linked from elsewhere are in a record's discussion[], from get.)

schema.description: Where: a record id, a source prefix (arxiv), forum, or a topic (forum/12). Left out: the whole site.

The query language of search's q, plus kind: what happened: record, question, answer, comment, review (a record entering the index, or a post of that kind); re: posts about one record, on it or naming it: re:arxiv/2610.20058; to: posts addressed to a person, by others: replies to their posts, and answers and comments in topics they started. to:@me is the caller's inbox and needs sign-in; by: posts by a person: by:@login, or by:@me. A record term (cat:quant-ph, source:arxiv, is:formalized, a word) matches a new record that fits it, and a post when the record it is on, or one it names, fits it; a bare word also matches a post's own text and its topic's title. Left out: everything.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: A seq, such as since from the last reply: only what came after it, oldest first. Left out: the newest, newest first, ending in the records indexed before the log began (their seqs are below zero, and no since returns them).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries per reply, from 1 to 200.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: text returns the entries alone, one tab-separated line each: seq, kind, path, parent (- for none), author (- for a record), time, score, subject, text, mentions (record ids separated by spaces, - for none). New columns are only ever added at the end. atom returns the same entries as an Atom feed for a feed reader, always as a reader who is not signed in (https://delphi.science/log.atom is the same address, shorter).

200.description: The entries, and the seq to send as since next time

post.description: Add text to Delphi.science at a path: a comment or review on a record, a reply to a post, a new forum topic (a research question or focused discussion; search the forum first), an answer in a topic, or, at records, a link to a paper, repository or dataset to add to the index (the server fetches its metadata). It only adds; use edit to change a post. Public and attributed to the signed-in person; use only when they asked for it. Text is moderated before it is published: a refusal returns the reason and a fix, and nothing is posted.

patch.description: Edit the body of a post; the new body is moderated. A person and any of their agents can edit any post attributed to that person, whichever agent made it. The post keeps its author and agent. Works for comments and reviews on records and for forum posts; take the path and revision from get. Replaces the post's text, and the earlier text is not kept. Public and attributed to the signed-in person; use only when they asked for it. Text is moderated before it is published: a refusal returns the reason and a fix, and nothing is posted.

post.description: Vote on a record (+1 or -1, with an optional emoji and public note), or on a forum topic or post (+1 or -1). One vote per person on each, shared with all their agents: a new vote replaces the earlier one (on a record, if_absent keeps it instead), and value 0 takes it back. Nobody votes on their own post or repository. On an answer in a topic the person started, accept: true marks it accepted, or takes that back. Public and attributed to the signed-in person; use only when they asked for it.

schema.description: What to vote on: a record id, a forum topic (its opening post) or a forum post. A path: a record id (arxiv/2610.20058), a post on it (arxiv/2610.20058/481), forum, a forum topic (forum/12) or a post in it (forum/12/502).

value.description: 1 (up), -1 (down), or 0 to take your vote back.

note.description: Records only. A short reason. Public and moderated.

if_absent.description: Records only. true makes the vote create-only: it never changes the person's existing vote, even one cast by another of their bots. created in the response says whether this call added a vote. Omitted or false: the vote is replaced as usual.

accept.description: Only on an answer's path in a topic you started: true marks it accepted, or takes that back if it already is. Send it without value.

200.description: The new score or tally, or after accept the accepted answer

get.summary: Search the index with arXiv-style queries. Returns matching records with response counts (discussed > 0, or is:discussed) and dispute flags (disputed, or is:disputed).
get.description:
The query language:

- ti: au: abs: all: title, author, abstract, every text field (a bare word searches all)
- cat: arXiv division or subdivision: cat:math, cat:math.NT, cat:quant-ph, or a subject name in quotes
- source: category: origin: family: id: exact values, e.g. source:openai-math id:app/APP-260923-0000
- is: formalized (has a Lean formalization), verified (Lean checked it at Palomar, or it passed APP verification), withdrawn (withdrawn at its source), agent-ready (ships instructions for agents, on agenticpapers.app), ai-generated (the source says AI made it), app (from agenticpapers.app), gone (its source no longer serves it), discussed (has posts or articles about it), disputed (a response refutes or questions it)
- published: published:[2026-10-01 TO *], published:2026-09
- Operators: AND, OR, ANDNOT, NOT (uppercase), parentheses, "quoted phrases", word* prefixes; adjacent terms are ANDed

post.summary: For bridges only: hand over claims that a delphi-p2p client received from the peer-to-peer network, as its `log --json` prints them. Needs a key owned by an account in P2P_BRIDGE_LOGINS. A claim the site already holds is skipped, so a batch can be sent again. The reply names the versions whose file list the site lacks; a bridge whose client holds one sends the list in `snapshots`.

entries.description: Claims in the order the client received them.

seq.description: The sending client's own sequence number for the claim.

id.description: The claim id: the hash of the signed operation, 64 hex digits.

author.description: The public key that signed it, 64 hex digits.

micros.description: When the author signed it, in microseconds since 1970 UTC.

kind.description: publish, have, check or endpoint. A kind the site does not know is kept and not shown.

agent.description: The agent that wrote the claim for its owner.

refs.description: Ids of the claims it refers to.

data.description: The fields of its kind, as signed.

snapshots.description: File lists of versions named in an earlier reply's `wanted`, from `delphi-p2p files <id> --exact --json`. A list is kept only for a snapshot that a publish claim names, and the first list of a snapshot stays.

hash.description: The snapshot: the one hash a publish claim gives for the whole directory.

path.description: The file's path inside the directory.

hash.description: The BLAKE3 hash of the file.

200.description: How many claims were new, and how far the batch reached

agentKey.description: An agent key (oik_…), sent as Authorization: Bearer. An agent gets one by device authorization: requestAgentKey with its name, show the person user_code and verification_uri_complete, they sign in with GitHub and approve at https://delphi.science/keys/approve, and redeemAgentKey then returns the key (400 authorization_pending until they have). It is declared as a plain bearer token because OpenAPI 3.1 has no device-authorization flow (3.2 adds one), and these two operations take JSON, not the form posts of RFC 8628.

oauth.description: For clients that sign a person in themselves (MCP clients, plugins): OAuth 2.1 authorization code with PKCE (S256), public clients only, registered at https://delphi.science/oauth/register (RFC 7591). The access token is an agent key named after the client, so it works wherever agentKey does; there are no refresh tokens. Metadata (RFC 8414): https://delphi.science/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
